goal: Better COVID and RSV weekly forecasts (Hub horizons 0-3, admissions and ED share) by fixing the nowcast of the two newest reported weeks, the main live failure, then expanding the tree from whatever wins.
history: Live diagnostics, 14 November entries of docs/challenges/covid.md and rsv.md: on the 14 Oct-4 Nov issuances scored against the Hub target data of 12 November, the RSV mixture (rsv-four, 40 fits) forecast too high (states/DC medians 1.09 x observed at full tree strength); log-admission pairwise relative WIS 0.768, rank 9 of 17, against 0.692 for RSVHub-ensemble; ED share 0.831, rank 8 of 10. Halving the trees (production correction_strength 0.5) is a stopgap. The COVID mixture (covid-gru-four, 40 fits) ranks 2nd on log admissions (0.409), but its 14 November US forecast was above every other Hub model, and on ED share it scores 0.909 against 0.810 for the ensemble. docs/experiments/reporting-delays-2026-27 (flu) shows why the trees overshoot: hospitals that report late add as much as before, but fewer states start below 80% coverage in 2026-27, so corrections learned from 2025-26 artificial errors are too large. The flu study nowcast-tree-20261113 tests the remedy; this study ports it to COVID and RSV.
data: data/processed/panel-coverage.npz (built 2026-11-13 from data/operational-20261111, truth day 2026-11-12, includes hosprep_flu/covid/rsv = hospitals reporting each pathogen's admissions, archived from 11 December 2024). RSV uses data/processed/panel-coverage-rsv.npz, the same panel with NHSN RSV admissions treated as unobserved before 2024-11-02 (as panel-rsv.npz). Dataset spec datasets/respiratory-us-weekly-coverage-cr.json adds hosprep_covid and hosprep_rsv sets. All references are refit on this panel; scores are not comparable with the covid-tree-20261030 or rsv-tree-20261013 numbers (different truth day, different evaluation inputs).

families.ref: The four submitted recipes per pathogen refit on the new panel, trees at full strength; plus the main root with no trees at forecast time (_raw).
families.T: Trees do the nowcast, learned from real archived report -> value 12 weeks later pairs (corrector_examples=real), reading hospital coverage of each corrected week (covariate_set=hosprep_<pathogen>, the network also reads it, error_signals=all). Variants: network trained on corrected histories (real_cov_hc), real pairs from every season (real_cov_all), coverage of all three pathogens (real_hosprep_all), MLP corrector pretrained on artificial errors (mlp_cov).
families.N: The network does the nowcast: no trees at forecast time (forecast_view=raw), artificial errors on every training episode at strength 1, learns the final values of recent weeks (reconstruction_labels), reads coverage.

roots.covid: Bh_wd (main root; width-256 direct-quantile MLP, neighbouring-state exchange, errors on half of episodes, weight decay), Ah (width-192 sampled MLP), pN_gru (GRU encoder, US-only summary), N_ms (finalized histories, multiscale features).
roots.rsv: Bw (main root; width-256 direct-quantile MLP, all six admission/ED histories), Ball_c0w512 (width 512, trained on actual archived reports), A4c0 (sampled MLP, Kinsa, no calendar), A4i (sampled MLP, all six histories).

selection_score: Primary: states/DC mean WIS of log(1 + admissions), October-May reference dates, Hub horizons 0-3, 2024-25 and 2025-26 equal; lower is better; per-seed average over seeds 44-47. Reported beside it: ED share WIS, US log WIS, interval coverage, ratio of medians to observed, and the forward problem.
expansion_rule: As nowcast-tree-20261113: four seeds per node; a child is better than its parent only if lower by more than the pooled seed noise (sd of seed-pair differences / sqrt 2); each round expands the best four nodes per pathogen and combines what helped; an axis is closed after two rounds of children all worse beyond noise. Finalists compared as seed mixtures, checked on the forward problem and replayed as all-season fits on the 2026-27 reports (live gate, horizons 0-1 only until later truth arrives).

The submitted releases' saved trees were reapplied to each 2026-27 Wednesday report (14 Oct-11 Nov) and each submitted median's log error split into the error of the corrected newest week and the error of the rise forecast from it. US admissions (sum of states/DC for the newest week): the first reports were 4-10% (RSV) and 5-10% (COVID) below the truth so far; the trees added 5-10% (RSV) and 4-5% (COVID); the corrected newest week ended -1% to +5% from the truth so far. The submitted medians were 7-19% above the truth for RSV from 21 October and 11-13% for COVID, almost all from the forecast rise (growth error +5% to +17% RSV, +12-13% COVID). Per state, mean |growth error| 0.37-0.56 (RSV) and 0.20-0.28 (COVID) in log(1+x) against 0.10-0.14 and 0.06-0.10 for the nowcast. Reading: the nowcast is roughly right and the excess comes from the network, consistent with double counting (networks trained on uncorrected histories with reconstruction labels learn the reporting uplift, then also receive corrected inputs). Newest weeks are still being revised up, so the nowcast errors will shift down a few percent and the growth share of the excess up.
